newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bad bank loans decreased in 1996 - study.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bad bank loans decreased in 1996 - study.

text.p: Bad loans by Argentine banks fell last year, according to a study by Veraz, a company that polls the finances of firms and individuals.
The study by Veraz, published in the daily Clarin Tuesday, found that 73 percent of bank loans were considered risk-free in October last year, the last month in which figures were available.
Some 11 percent of bank loans were considered irretrievable and a further six percent were seen as high-risk loans in October 1996.
Those figures compare with similar statistics for November 1995, when 67 percent of bank loans were seen as risk-free, 11 percent were deemed irretrievable and nine percent were high-risk loans.

Veraz said the improvement by companies and individuals in paying off their debts came hand in hand with the economic rebound and the rebound had increased the possibilities for firms to raise funds in the international credit markets.
